summary: CKGSB's marketing team is in execution mode on the seven-month SEO/AI-search strategy, with Asia Star and the new Intelligent China program as the clear top priorities, while the knowledge website redesign and a cluster of October events and content deliverables demand immediate attention.
summaryDetail: The single most important thing right now is operational: an Outlook account lockout caused by stale saved passwords across devices must be resolved by updating credentials everywhere and confirming the backend unlock with JSB, or it will keep disrupting the team. The big initiative in motion is the seven-month SEO/AI-search visibility strategy, where Asia Star and Intelligent China outrank US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley put on hold for Q1, with Berkeley possibly entering the audit phase); Joseph's target areas/prompts document, analysis of Asia Star participant profiles and CRM hot leads, the Intelligent China webpage launch, and Google Ads conversion tracking are the critical path. The knowledge website redesign is also live: the team agreed to combine elements from both design concepts, keep the knowledge menu centered with the school menu at top, include BCI and BSI indices on the homepage, and remove the standalone video section in favor of topic integration—Joseph needs to share the HTML file and a 30-minute feedback meeting must be scheduled. This week's urgent items include finalizing the MBA new-intake social post with a ceremony photo, sending updated APEC event briefings to CZC, sharing completed English case studies with Global Marcom, dispatching the SwissCham forum cooperation email, and deciding on Pascal Lamy fireside chat attendance and the Chinese name for the Women in Leadership event. Upcoming work includes Asia Start May Edition marketing assets (Andrea and Katya spotlight videos for LinkedIn, YouTube, and website), while the ESG report remains on the back burner and the team must avoid using 论坛 in event names going forward due to government review procedures.
